newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says Hun Sen agrees to talk with royalists.
newsitem.headline: Japan says Hun Sen agrees to talk with royalists.

text.p: Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen has agreed to open talks with forces of his rival First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh to end fighting in Phnom Penh, a Japanese Foreign Ministry statement said on Sunday.
The statement said the president of Cambodia's parliament Chea Sim told Japan's ambassador in Phnom Penh of the possible peace development in a meeting on Sunday.
It said the planned talks would involve Hun Sen, Chea Sim, a military representative of Prince Norodom Ranariddh, and First Vice-President Loy Simchheang, an ally of the prince.
Heavy fighting rocked the Cambodian capital on Sunday as forces loyal to the rival prime ministers battled for a second day and thousands of people fled the city.
Japan, the biggest aid donor to Cambodia, has stepped in with a flurry of diplomatic activity to end the crisis.

Japanese officials said Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto had ordered his embassy in Phnom Penh to send a message to Cambodia's King Norodom Sihanouk, believed to be in Beijing, asking him to help end the fighting. Japan has also urged Hun Sen to take the lead in trying to find a peaceful solution.
